overview.text:
Vale brings Google documentation style checks into your editing workflow.
Install the plugin in Claude Code or Codex to get automatic checks, an
on-demand checking command, and shared writing skills.

[Install Vale](installation.html) · [Try the examples](usage.html) ·
[Browse the source](https://github.com/swack-tools/vale-ai-plugin)

projects.summary: Google documentation style checks for Claude Code and Codex.

blocks.text:
| Interface | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Automatic hooks | Enabled plugin hooks | Enabled and trusted plugin hooks |
| On-demand review | `/vale:check-prose` | `$vale:check-prose` or `/skills` |
| Procedural guidance | `/vale:procedural-prose` | `$vale:procedural-prose` or `/skills` |
| Writing guidance | `/vale:google-prose` | `$vale:google-prose` or `/skills` |
| Legacy prompt command | Use the checking skill | `/prompts:vale` on legacy clients only |

Claude Code exposes plugin skills as namespaced slash commands. Codex supports
skill mentions and a skill picker. Its optional custom prompt command requires
the [separate user installation](installation.html#legacy-slash-command-compatibility).
Codex 0.158.0 doesn't recognize custom prompt commands. Use `/skills` or a
skill mention on that version. The clients don't use identical command syntax.

Install Python 3.11+, Vale 3.23+, and Claude Code or Codex with plugin and
lifecycle hook support. The runtime supports macOS, Linux, and Windows Subsystem for Linux. Native
Windows isn't supported because state locking uses `fcntl`.

Tested with Codex 0.158.0, Claude Code 2.1.277, and Vale 3.23.0. Hooks run on the
machine that holds the workspace. Install Python and Vale there.

```sh
# macOS
brew install python vale
python3 --version
vale --version
```

### Optional markup parsers

Markdown and source comments use Vale's built-in parsers. Install these tools
only if your project uses the corresponding markup format:

| Format | Package | Required command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| reStructuredText: `.rst` | Python Docutils | `rst2html` |
| AsciiDoc: `.adoc` | Ruby Asciidoctor | `asciidoctor` |

Install Docutils in a Python environment available to the agent:

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install docutils
export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"
rst2html --version
```

With Ruby installed, install Asciidoctor:

```sh
gem install asciidoctor
asciidoctor --version
```

Ensure the agent's process inherits the parser commands on `PATH`. Restart the
agent after changing its environment. A missing parser prevents that format's
check from completing. It doesn't mean the document has no findings.

For Linux and Windows Subsystem for Linux, use the [Vale installation guide](https://vale.sh/docs/install).
Vale needs no account or API key. Review the package scripts before enabling
hooks. Choose one installation method per workspace to avoid duplicate feedback.

Its tools read viewing history, recommendations, titles, lists, and calendars, or make explicitly requested changes with write permission. Each person authorizes their own Trakt account through client OAuth 2.0 and device approval. Existing tokens and standalone device login remain read-only; client OAuth 2.0 reauthorization is required for write scope. The server supplies tools; standalone skills supply workflow instructions and require this connection.

Terminal & desktop Code

Claude Code

Install from the marketplace

Run these commands in your terminal:

claude plugin marketplace add swack-tools/trakt-ai-plugin
claude plugin install trakt-mcp@trakt-mcp

Start a new Claude Code session. Open /mcp, select the plugin’s Trakt server, and authenticate. Complete the device-code walkthrough below.

In the Claude desktop app’s local Code sessions, use + → Plugins → Add plugin after adding the marketplace. User-scoped command-line tool installs are also available to local desktop Code sessions on the same computer. Hosted sessions have different plugin availability.

Or add the server directly

claude mcp add --transport http trakt https://trakt.swacktech.com/mcp

Open /mcp in Claude Code to authenticate. The command defaults to the local project scope; add --scope user if you want the direct server available across projects.

Update the plugin

claude plugin marketplace update trakt-mcp
claude plugin update trakt-mcp@trakt-mcp

Start a new session after updating.

Official guidance: Claude Code plugin installation and scopes.

Fifteen MCP tools include six focused tools for public list discovery, list items, calendars, and personal list creation or item edits. The existing catalog tools still cover other documented API operations. Focused list writes require explicit confirmation, write authorization, and ownership verification. Successful calls include typed `structuredContent` while retaining the original JSON text for older clients. Catalog coverage does not mean every operation is callable; inspect an operation before using generic read/write tools. See the [API reference](https://trakt.swacktech.com/reference.html#api-coverage).

New browser OAuth connections request read and write access when scope is omitted, and the consent page states those permissions. Explicit `trakt:read` requests stay read-only. Existing tokens and standalone device login remain read-only; reauthorize through your client with `trakt:read trakt:write` for writes. Refresh cannot increase scope. The write tool also requires `confirmed: true` for a concrete change the user requested. Skills verify changes through reads and never automatically repeat a write after an uncertain failure.

Use natural language

Describe the outcome you want. Your client can select an appropriate installed skill; clients with explicit skill invocation can also select it by name. Claude Code exposes plugin skills under the plugin namespace, such as /trakt-mcp:what-to-watch. Client interfaces and availability vary.

Each watched request reads one compact page, retaining identifying metadata, genres, counts, and timestamps while reducing response size. Full detail is available for specific metadata needs. All-history workflows continue until every next page is exhausted. They provide progress updates and report partial coverage if interrupted. Recent viewing and ordinary title lookup stay bounded. Workflows stop on unavailable capabilities and treat movie descriptions and other remote text as data. Read workflows never modify your account. Write workflows require a concrete user request, trakt:write permission, and confirmed: true. Existing read-only connections need client reauthorization. A clear request supplies intent; the skill asks only for missing decisions. Login tools also change connection state.

usage.notes: Install the repository marketplace or add the remote MCP server, then authenticate through the client's MCP controls. For skill use, natural language or /trakt-mcp:what-to-watch is documented; /mcp manages the server connection, not skill invocation.

overview.text:
CODEX + CLAUDE · TOKEN AUDIT

Evidence before
optimization.

Understand where your tokens go.
Find changes worth testing.

Review your session and available project to find evidence-backed ways to use fewer tokens. The command checks instruction bloat, repeated exploration, large tool outputs, long files/functions, plugins/MCP, and model-routing rules. It returns a report in chat with concrete proposals and validation steps.

It does not equate “smaller file,” “cheaper model,” or “more plugins” with proven savings. Actual usage comes from session counters. Recommendations are labeled measured, estimated, or hypothesis.

No runtime hooks are installed. See the implementation review, reproducible benchmark and research for measured reductions, added overhead, and the limits of quality claims.

Measured

What the log or file actually records.

Estimated

A calculation with explicit assumptions.

Hypothesis

A proposed change that needs a test.

projects.name: Colab Pilot

overview.text:
Zero-waste Google Colab orchestration for Antigravity, Claude Code, and Codex. Stage large datasets to Google Drive at zero Compute Unit cost, provision BF16 GPU cascades, launch detached jobs resilient to WebSocket drops, and guard against orphaned sessions.

Read the [full documentation and workflow guide](https://colab.ai.swacktech.com/) for setup walkthroughs, architecture details, and tool specifications.

projects.summary: Zero-waste Google Colab orchestration with GPU cascade provisioning, Drive staging, detached jobs, and Compute Unit leak hooks.

blocks.text:
- **Antigravity**: Install with `agy plugin install https://github.com/swack-tools/colab-pilot-plugin` and invoke `/colab-pilot`, `/colab-train`, `/colab-shard-cpu`, or `/colab-watch`.
- **Claude Code**: Add `swack-tools/ai-plugin-marketplace` and install `colab-pilot@swack-tools-community`. Invoke `/colab-pilot:colab-pilot` or ask Claude to manage your Colab run.
- **Codex**: Add `https://github.com/swack-tools/ai-plugin-marketplace.git` and install `colab-pilot@swack-tools-community`. Invoke `$colab-pilot` or `$colab-train` in chat.

See the [installation and client setup guide](https://colab.ai.swacktech.com/install.html) for detailed walkthroughs and headless Google Drive configuration.
